Attackers are impersonating popular AI products to distribute malware, steal browser sessions, and compromise business accounts. ANY.RUN linked 1,258 public sandbox analyses to fake AI campaigns between April and October of 2026.

The campaigns also increase operational pressure on MSSPs serving US businesses, which accounted for 16% of country-attributed targets.

Similar attacks appearing across different customers can trigger repetitive investigations, consume analyst capacity, and extend response times, making it harder to maintain consistent service levels as threat activity grows.

How Fake AI Attacks Are Reaching US Businesses

Fake AI attacks pose a serious risk to business security

The campaigns investigated by ANY.RUN use familiar AI brands to encourage employees to execute malicious commands, install compromised applications, or submit credentials through fraudulent authentication pages.

Attackers impersonate Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, and other AI services. Their lures appear in sponsored search results, legitimate hosting services, shared AI conversations, and counterfeit download websites.

Fake Copilot installation page

One campaign impersonating Claude demonstrates how easily a routine software installation can become an infection.

In the attack analyzed through ANY.RUN's Interactive Sandbox, the victim encounters a page resembling the official Claude download website. Clicking the Windows download button copies a command to the clipboard and displays instructions for executing it through PowerShell.

Instead of installing the expected application, the command launches mshta.exe, retrieves a malicious HTA file, and triggers an encoded PowerShell execution chain.

Completed analyses exposed infostealer activity
ANY.RUN’s Sandbox revealed the entire infection chain

The technique presents a difficult detection scenario. The employee initiates the process voluntarily, the attack relies on legitimate Windows utilities, and the malicious payload appears only after several execution stages.

For MSSPs managing multiple customer environments, this creates a recurring operational challenge: the initial indicators vary, while the underlying attacker behavior remains similar.

Why Fake AI Campaigns Put Pressure on MSSP Operations

ANY.RUN data shows that 16% of Fake AI attacks were directed at the US

An individual fake AI incident may appear straightforward once its full execution chain is visible. The operational difficulty increases when an MSSP must recognize similar activity across customers with different technologies, policies, and risk profiles.

These campaigns create pressure on three interconnected SOC processes.

  • Monitoring and detection coverage: Attackers constantly rotate domains, hosting services, and AI brands, making new campaign variants harder to detect with existing indicators.
  • Triage and escalation management: Evasive attack chains require deeper investigation, increasing analyst workload, response times, and unnecessary escalations.
  • Threat hunting and detection improvement: Findings from individual investigations need to be correlated and reused to strengthen detection across customer environments.

These challenges directly affect the metrics MSSP leadership manages: MTTD, MTTR, escalation rates, investigation cost, and SLA compliance.

Improving those metrics requires a coordinated approach to monitoring, investigation, and intelligence reuse.

Improving Tier 1 Efficiency Through Behavioral Investigation

The first opportunity is to reduce the time analysts spend establishing whether suspicious activity represents a genuine threat.

Fake AI campaigns illustrate why this matters. A suspicious download page may appear harmless until the analyst clicks the installation button or follows the instructions. Static inspection can provide an incomplete picture of the resulting execution chain.

ANY.RUN's Interactive Sandbox enables analysts to reproduce these interactions in an isolated environment and observe the resulting processes, network activity, and malicious behavior.

Instead of sending ambiguous cases directly to experienced analysts, Tier 1 teams can use behavioral evidence to determine whether a threat requires containment, further investigation, or closure.

Reducing unnecessary escalations improves the distribution of work across SOC tiers. Senior analysts can concentrate on complex investigations, while junior analysts resolve a larger proportion of routine cases independently.

For MSSP leadership, this creates an opportunity to maintain investigation quality and SLA performance as customer alert volumes increase.

Expanding Detection Coverage Across Customer Environments

Efficient triage addresses threats that have already generated suspicion. MSSPs also need to identify emerging campaigns early enough to reduce the number of successful compromises.

Fake AI attacks demonstrate how quickly isolated indicators lose value. Landing domains change, while malicious infrastructure and behavioral patterns may persist across multiple campaign variants.

This makes continuously updated, validated threat intelligence particularly important for MSSPs.

Strengthening Proactive Defense with Effective Threat Hunting

The next opportunity is to ensure that individual investigations contribute to broader detection improvements.

ANY.RUN researchers identified several recurring behaviors across the fake AI campaigns, including suspicious PowerShell installation commands, mshta.exe execution, encoded download instructions, and scheduled tasks launching browsers for session theft.

These patterns provide useful starting points for hunting related activity beyond the original incident.

TI Lookup shows how a malicious domain is linked to other attacker infrastructure

Threat Intelligence Lookup helps analysts investigate relationships between suspicious indicators, malware behavior, historical sightings, and associated campaign infrastructure.

When an analyst identifies a fake AI infection affecting one customer, the team can investigate associated infrastructure, determine which behavioral indicators remain relevant, and use those findings to search for related activity in other customer environments.

The results can also inform detection engineering, allowing teams to update their rules based on observed attacker behavior rather than relying exclusively on newly identified domains.

ANY.RUN's Threat Intelligence solutions provide access to 24 times more IOCs per incident, expanding the evidence available for correlation and hunting.

Over time, this process helps MSSPs improve detection coverage using knowledge already generated through daily investigations.

How ANY.RUN Helps MSSPs Improve Detection and Response Across Clients

ANY.RUN combines Interactive Sandbox and Threat Intelligence to help MSSPs strengthen monitoring, triage, and threat hunting across customer environments. Together, these solutions improve detection coverage, reduce investigation workload, and make threat intelligence reusable across clients.

The operational impact includes:

  • Earlier threat detection: 36% higher detection rate and up to 58% more threats identified, helping MSSPs strengthen protection across customers.
  • Faster investigations: 21 minutes faster response, allowing analysts to process more cases while maintaining SLA performance.
  • Fewer escalations: 30% fewer Tier 1 to Tier 2 escalations, preserving senior analyst capacity for complex incidents.
  • More effective threat hunting: Sandbox evidence and Threat Intelligence Lookup help MSSPs identify related attacks and reuse findings across customer environments.

For MSSP leadership, these improvements translate into lower investigation costs, reduced risk of major client incidents, and more consistent SLA performance. By reducing repetitive work and applying intelligence across customers, MSSPs can scale their services without proportionally increasing analyst headcount, improving operational margins while maintaining protection quality.

Conclusion

Fake AI campaigns demonstrate how attackers can exploit familiar software brands, legitimate infrastructure, and routine employee activity to reach corporate environments.

For MSSPs, the long-term challenge is maintaining detection effectiveness as these campaigns evolve and appear across different customer environments.

The strongest operational response combines early threat intelligence, efficient behavioral investigation, and systematic reuse of findings across monitoring and threat hunting.

With these processes working together, MSSPs can improve detection coverage, reduce investigation overhead, maintain more consistent service levels, and protect a growing customer base with greater operational efficiency.
